executive_summary: HARNESS (Golf-5 specimen 1df1a3f5, coordinator row 2158bc68): lib/sub-agents/resolve-repo.js's applySubAgentRepoVerdict() downgrades a sub-agent's verdict from PASS to CONDITIONAL_PASS on repo-resolution failure, but never populates results.conditions/results.justification -- both required (non-empty array / >=50 chars) by sub_agent_execution_results' check_conditions_required and check_justification_required CHECK constraints whenever verdict='CONDITIONAL_PASS'. Any caller that stores a downgraded row without separately synthesizing these fields hits Postgres 23514 and the row is never written -- the writer defeats the very SUB_AGENT_REPO_RESOLUTION gate it exists to serve. LEAD-phase Explore (evidence 8881cb8f, dual-agent verified) traced this to THREE concrete, file:line-confirmed defects: (1) applySubAgentRepoVerdict itself never sets conditions/justification -- already mitigated for callers routed through lib/sub-agent-executor/results-storage.js's deriveConditionalPassEvidence (QF-20260603-485) but NOT for callers that bypass it; (2) lib/sub-agents/regression.js's storeResults() hand-rolls its own INSERT that omits metadata/conditions/justification entirely, AND (found by adversarial VALIDATION re-review) calls storeResults() BEFORE applySubAgentRepoVerdict() runs -- so even a correctly-shaped results object would have its mutation persisted too late to ever reach the DB row; (3) regression.js's execute() calls resolveSubAgentRepo() with targetApplication:options.target_application, which the CLI entry point never populates, and getSDDetails() didn't even SELECT the target_application column -- so every CLI-invoked run unconditionally resolves {repoPath:null,repoResolved:false,registrySource:'fallback'} regardless of the actual worktree/registry state. PIVOT (documented, not silently applied): the SD's original description also proposed 'preserve executed_from_cwd instead of nulling repo_path on failure' -- investigation found this would be actively harmful: v_sub_agent_repo_compliance classifies a row 'cwd_leak' (or, per VALIDATION's sharper correction, silently reclassifies to 'healthy' when toplevel-compatible -- a FALSE GREEN, worse than a false block) whenever metadata->>'repo_path' equals executed_from_cwd. The existing repo_resolved:false field is already the gate-consumed explicit failure marker; no repo_path change was made.

functional_requirements.title: applySubAgentRepoVerdict() populates conditions/justification on every downgrade, making its output insertable by construction
functional_requirements.description: lib/sub-agents/resolve-repo.js:227-273 applySubAgentRepoVerdict() downgrades PASS->CONDITIONAL_PASS (lines 257-270 pre-fix) via recordVerdictMutation, pushing only a warnings entry. database/migrations/20251115114444_add_validation_modes_to_sub_agent_results.sql's check_conditions_required (conditions non-null non-empty jsonb array) and check_justification_required (justification non-null, >=50 chars) both apply whenever verdict='CONDITIONAL_PASS' -- neither is populated, so any INSERT of a downgraded row not otherwise mitigated violates 23514. Fix, guarded to fire ONLY inside the existing downgrade branch (not on skipVerdictAdjust or a legitimate skip_reason path, matching VALIDATION's scoping note): if results.conditions is missing/empty, set it to a single {action: <degradation reason>, priority:'medium', blocking:false} entry; if results.justification is missing or <50 chars, set it to a descriptive string built from the same degradation reason. A caller-supplied conditions/justification (already present and valid) is left untouched -- this is additive synthesis, not an override, mirroring lib/sub-agent-executor/results-storage.js's deriveConditionalPassEvidence pass-through contract. Explicitly does NOT touch metadata.repo_path -- see FR-4 for why.
acceptance_criteria: A resolution shaped exactly like the Golf-5 specimen ({repoPath:null, repoResolved:false, registrySource:'fallback'}) applied to a PASS-verdict results object yields verdict='CONDITIONAL_PASS' with a non-empty results.conditions array and a results.justification string >=50 chars.

A JS-level mirror of both CHECK constraints (conditions non-empty array + justification length>=50, only enforced when verdict='CONDITIONAL_PASS') passes against the mutated results object -- proving the row would not violate 23514 without needing a live DB round-trip.

No conditions/justification are added when the resolution is healthy (repoResolved:true, no probe failure) or when skipReason/skipVerdictAdjust apply -- verdict and results object are otherwise unchanged from current behavior.
An already-populated caller-supplied conditions/justification is preserved verbatim, not overwritten.
Mutation-verified: reverting this fix makes the Golf-5-specimen insertability test fail; restoring it passes.

functional_requirements.title: regression.js: apply the repo verdict BEFORE storing results, and forward metadata/conditions/justification into the insert
functional_requirements.description: lib/sub-agents/regression.js:265 (pre-fix) calls storeResults(sdId, results) INSIDE the main try block; applySubAgentRepoVerdict(results, resolution) ran afterward, unconditionally, at line 278 -- AFTER the row was already persisted. This means the repo-resolution verdict/metadata mutation had ZERO effect on what actually reached the DB (found by adversarial VALIDATION re-review of the initial LEAD plan, which had proposed only the insert-payload fix in isolation). Separately, storeResults()'s own INSERT payload (lines 776-788 pre-fix) omitted metadata/conditions/justification entirely, so even a correctly-timed mutation would still be dropped. Fix: call applySubAgentRepoVerdict(results, resolution) exactly ONCE, immediately after resolution is obtained (before Phase 1 begins) -- this is also the semantically correct place, since later phases (test/API/coverage comparison) only escalate the verdict toward FAIL and never downgrade PASS back from a prior CONDITIONAL_PASS, so applying the repo-resolution fail-closed check first composes correctly with the substantive checks that follow. Remove the two now-redundant later calls (the capture-baseline early-return branch and the end-of-function call). Add metadata/conditions/justification to storeResults()'s insert payload.
acceptance_criteria: applySubAgentRepoVerdict is called exactly once per execute() invocation, before storeResults runs (for the main full-validation/compare path) or before the capture-baseline early return.
storeResults()'s insert payload includes metadata, conditions, and justification sourced from results.

For a resolution shaped like the Golf-5 specimen, the row storeResults() would attempt to insert satisfies both CHECK constraints (same JS-mirrored assertion as FR-1, applied to the constructed insert payload).

functional_requirements.title: regression.js: resolve target_application from the SD before calling resolveSubAgentRepo (fixes the true root cause of the Golf-5 specimen)
functional_requirements.description: regression.js:83-88 (pre-fix) passed targetApplication:options.target_application to resolveSubAgentRepo, called BEFORE getSDDetails(sdId) (line 97 pre-fix) -- which itself didn't SELECT target_application at all (line 290 pre-fix: `.select('id, title, sd_type, intensity_level, status')`), and the CLI entry point (lines 795-814 pre-fix) never populates options.target_application. Confirmed (Explore + VALIDATION, independently): for ANY CLI invocation, resolveSubAgentRepo's `candidate` (resolve-repo.js:165) is unconditionally undefined, producing {repoPath:null,repoResolved:false,registrySource:'fallback'} regardless of whether the worktree/registry would resolve correctly -- structurally blind, not failure-dependent. Fix: move the getSDDetails(sdId) call to before resolveSubAgentRepo, add target_application to its SELECT, and pass resolveTargetApplicationForRegression(options, sdDetails) (a new pure, exported precedence helper: options.target_application wins, else sdDetails.target_application, else undefined) as resolveSubAgentRepo's targetApplication. Also normalize sdId (via the already-imported normalizeSDId) inside getSDDetails before the `.eq('id', ...)` lookup -- the `id` column is uuid, and a caller passing an sd_key would otherwise return zero rows (VALIDATION-flagged latent bug in the naive fix).
acceptance_criteria: getSDDetails's SELECT includes target_application, and its lookup is normalized (sd_key or UUID input both resolve).

resolveTargetApplicationForRegression(options, sdDetails) is exported and unit-tested for all four precedence cases (options wins; falls back to sdDetails; both absent returns undefined; null sdDetails is safe).
getSDDetails is now called before resolveSubAgentRepo in execute(), and its target_application feeds the resolution call via the precedence helper.

functional_requirements.title: Do NOT alias metadata.repo_path to executed_from_cwd on resolution failure (documented pivot, not a code change)
functional_requirements.description: The SD's original description proposed 'on registry miss, preserve the measured executed_from_cwd [as metadata.repo_path] and mark resolution failure explicitly, instead of clobbering with a canonicalized null.' Investigated and REJECTED after two independent adversarial passes: database/migrations/20260604_fix_v_sub_agent_repo_compliance_case_insensitive.sql's v_sub_agent_repo_compliance view CASE statement checks `metadata->>'repo_path' IS NULL` -> 'explicit_null' BEFORE checking `metadata->>'repo_path' = executed_from_cwd` -> 'cwd_leak' -- so today's null repo_path already classifies as the gate-appropriate explicit_null/explicit_null_intra (correctly distinguishing intra- vs cross-repo per scripts/modules/handoff/executors/plan-to-exec/gates/sub-agent-repo-resolution.js). Aliasing repo_path to executed_from_cwd on every registry miss would make every such row non-null and equal to executed_from_cwd, hitting the cwd_leak branch instead -- which the gate's own toplevel-compatibility check (QF-20260528-426, lines 100-118 of the gate file) RECLASSIFIES TO 'healthy' whenever the writer's cwd is toplevel-compatible with the expected repo. That means aliasing would not merely over-block; for the common intra-repo case it would manufacture a FALSE GREEN -- masking the exact failure this SD exists to make visible. No code change: the existing metadata.repo_resolved:false field (already unconditionally set, already read by the gate's classifyRow for the unresolved/unresolved_intra branches) already IS the explicit, gate-consumed resolution-failure marker the success criteria ask for.
acceptance_criteria: A new regression-guard unit test asserts metadata.repo_path stays null (not aliased to executed_from_cwd) on a registry-miss resolution, and that repo_path never equals executed_from_cwd for this case.
The PRD/handoff record documents this pivot explicitly (this FR) so a future reader does not re-attempt the aliasing fix without re-deriving the same cwd_leak/false-green analysis.

technical_requirements.title: No schema/migration change
technical_requirements.description: conditions/justification columns and their CHECK constraints already exist. This SD is pure application-code (resolve-repo.js, regression.js) + test additions. No new columns, no new RPC, no migration file, no change to v_sub_agent_repo_compliance or the SUB_AGENT_REPO_RESOLUTION gate.

technical_requirements.description: applySubAgentRepoVerdict(results, resolution, opts) keeps its existing signature and mutate-in-place contract; api.js/dependency.js/performance.js/design/index.js/security.js (which route through the canonical lib/sub-agent-executor/results-storage.js writer, confirmed unaffected by Explore) require no changes. regression.js's execute(sdId, subAgent, options) keeps its existing signature and {verdict,...} return shape.

No new false-positive (cwd_leak) or false-negative (healthy-reclassification) gate outcomes are introduced by this fix.

risks.risk: Moving applySubAgentRepoVerdict's call site earlier in regression.js's execute() changes WHEN the repo-resolution downgrade is visible to later phases -- a later phase could theoretically read results.verdict expecting 'PASS' and behave differently.
risks.mitigation: Traced every later phase's verdict-mutation logic: test/import failures always force FAIL regardless of current verdict; API/coverage branches only escalate PASS->CONDITIONAL_PASS (already a no-op if verdict is already CONDITIONAL_PASS) or FAIL unconditionally on breaking changes. No phase reads verdict for any purpose other than escalating it, so reordering is safe.

risks.mitigation: Flagged as an out-of-scope completion-flag finding for a follow-up ticket, not fixed here, to keep this SD's diff scoped to the repo-writer mechanism its title names.

system_architecture.summary: Two-file application-code fix: the shared canonical writer (resolve-repo.js) gains defensive conditions/justification synthesis on its own downgrade branch; the one hand-rolled-insert caller that bypasses the canonical storage path (regression.js) gets its call ordering and insert payload corrected, plus a small exported precedence helper for target_application resolution. No new components.
